title: Customer network fallback + audit-sampling experiment
body:
Context

This is an exploratory PRD for two related features for Private deployments: (1) a controlled, auditable fallback path when Redwood cannot reach a customer-managed network endpoint (VPC/on-prem), and (2) a lightweight, risk-aware sampling engine for audit-log retention and SIEM exports. The goal is to give enterprise customers predictable availability during transient networking failures while preserving forensic fidelity and minimizing cost/PII exposure.

Motivation / problems we're solving

- Customers with private deployments often rely on customer-managed control-plane or telemetry endpoints (syslog/SIEM) which can be intermittently unreachable. Current behavior (hard-fail or silent drop) either breaks operator workflows or loses critical evidence.
- Audit logs for Private deployments are large and expensive to store/retain at full fidelity for all events. Many events are low-value noise; however, when an incident happens we must ensure we retained sufficient evidence to reconstruct root cause.
- Approval gates (customer-initiated changes, network handoffs) need both timely operator action and an immutable evidence record that can be compact but provably complete for the event class.

Design principles

- Safety-first: Never create an automatic silent bypass that jeopardizes customer intent without explicit policy. Fallbacks must be discoverable, reversible, and cryptographically attested.
- Evidence minimization: Keep compact representations for low-risk events; preserve full payloads for high-risk / sampled events.
- Customer sovereignty: Configurable sampling and fallback policies owned by the customer; we provide sane defaults and templates for regulated industries.
- Auditability: All fallback decisions and sampling choices must be recorded with causal metadata (policy id, risk score, operator id, timestamp, and compact proof).

Success metrics (initial target)

- Mean time-to-reconnect for customer-managed endpoints reduced (for customer perceived availability) by 30% via fallback while still recording evidence of outage.
- Forensic recall: In synthetic incident replays, sampled corpus must include the root-cause event 98% of the time given configured risk thresholds.
- Cost control: Average audit-store size per deployment reduced by 40% vs full-fidelity retention at 90-day window for typical traffic mixes.
- Operator UX: 90% of SRE/Customer operators are able to locate fallback attestations in the console within 3 clicks.

Non-goals

- Not a full SIEM replacement. We provide connectors and sampled exports, but we will not attempt to implement cross-customer correlation or advanced SOAR capabilities in this phase.
- Not solving permanent misconfigurations — long-term offline fixes require standard onboarding and runbook steps.

Feature components (high level)

1) Network Fallback Modes (policy-driven)
- Reject (strict): Fail requests and surface immediate error to callers. Record failure with full evidence.
- Buffered Queue (soft-fail): Accept inbound requests for a configurable short window (e.g., 5–30s) and attempt local retry/queueing; attach a temporary opaque receipt and emit evidence when exported.
- Proxy Bypass (graceful-fallback): For customer-allowed endpoints, route to Redwood-managed compatible endpoint variant (e.g., hosted telemetry sink) for short periods. This requires customer opt-in and cryptographic attestation.
- Emergency Allow (operator-confirm): A time-limited operator-initiated bypass that requires multi-party confirmation in the console and generates an immutable audit bundle.

Policy primitives
- Policy id and version (immutable reference).
- Allowed fallback modes (enum).
- Max fallback duration and retry window.
- Risk thresholds driving sampling decisions.
- Trusted operator list and escalation chains.

2) Risk-aware Sampling Engine
- Event classification: quick stateless classifier that assigns an event-level risk score based on change type (network-change, credential-rotation, approval, heartbeat), actor (operator, automated job, customer API), and context (time-of-day, region, recent-failure-rate).
- Sampling policies: deterministic rules (e.g., sample 100% for risk >= 0.85; 10% for 0.25–0.85; 0.5% for < 0.25), plus a configurable reservoir sampler to bound storage use.
- Stitching tokens: sampled items include a compact token that allows later retrieval of neighboring low-signal events (within window) to reconstruct causal chains without retaining everything.
- Ephemeral cache: short-term high-fidelity cache (30–120m) for rapid forensic flips; long-term archive only contains sampled/full items per policy.

3) Evidence Capsule (compact schema)
- Capsule id (UUID), policy_id, fallback_decision, risk_score, timestamps, signing_operator (if present), ktrace (trace id list), and compact diffs of the payload (redacted where PII).
- Capsule stored in two forms: (a) compact JSON summary for immediate console queries, and (b) encrypted blob in cold storage (S3/GCS) if the capsule is flagged as retained full-fidelity.
- All capsules have an associated signature created by Redwood HSM/KMS + customer-provided public key when configured (supporting BYOK).

4) Approval Gate UX and Console flow
- Approval card: shows incoming change, estimated risk, recommended fallback behavior, and one-click operator actions (approve, require-more-info, escalate).
- Emergency bypass flow: explicit 2-of-3 operator confirmation, auto-expiry, and automated rollback hook. UI surfaces signed evidence capsule link for auditors.

APIs and Integrations
- New control-plane APIs: POST /policies/{id}/simulate, GET /evidence/{capsule_id}, POST /fallbacks/{deployment}/override (operator-only).
- Export connectors: syslog, HTTP-webhook, SIEM-forwarder (CEF), with configurable sampling mappings to preserve formats.
- KMS/HSM integrations: support for Redwood-managed KMS by default; BYOK customer-wrapped keys for capsule signing.

Rollout plan (phased)
- Phase 0 (experiments): internal-only A/B on 5 dev-private deployments + synthetic network failure injection.
- Phase 1 (alpha): selected small customers opt-in: enable buffered-queue + 10% sampling. Gather SRE and customer feedback.
- Phase 2 (beta): add proxy-bypass and emergency-allow with console flows + additional SIEM connectors.
- Phase 3 (GA): policy templates for regulated verticals, BYOK signing enabled, SLA addendum options for fallback guarantees.

Operational considerations
- Monitoring: new SLOs for fallback frequency, time-in-fallback, and evidence-export latency. Dashboards for per-customer sampling rates and storage footprint.
- Cost accounting: per-capsule billing bucket when full-fidelity blobs are retained; sampled compact events billed at a lower retention tier.
- Security: ensure signed capsules use secure key lifecycle; require operator MFA for emergency bypass actions.

Open questions / risks
- Legal: Is proxy-bypass acceptable under customer contracts/regulatory regimes? We need legal sign-off and optional consent flow.
- Forensics completeness: What is the minimum tokenization strategy that allows root-cause reconstruction for the majority of incidents? We must run red-team reconstructions with multiple customers.
- Latency/throughput: Buffered queue and proxy-bypass add complexity to the serving runtime; we need perf-budgeting and fallbacks for high-throughput tenants.

Next steps (short-term tasks)
- [A] Implement a minimal capsule schema and a signing prototype (eng-applied-ml + infra).
- [B] Build a simulator for network failures and evaluate sampling recall on historical private-deploy traces.
- [C] Draft legal addendum language for proxy-bypass and emergency operator allow.
- [D] Design console mockups for emergency bypass two-party flow and evidence browse UX (product + devx).

Appendix: quick scenarios
- Scenario 1 (Telemetry sink unreachable): customer syslog endpoint times out. Policy: buffered queue (15s) + sample 20% full payload. Outcome: callers receive transient 503 until queueers hold request; evidence capsule created with compressed payload and retry metadata. If buffered queue exceeds threshold, a proxy-bypass is attempted (if allowed) and recorded.
- Scenario 2 (Operator emergency allow): operator triggers temporary bypass to push credential-rotation that would otherwise be blocked by network gating. Two other operators confirm; bypass is allowed for 12 minutes and then auto-rolled back. Evidence capsule contains operator signatures and the exact diffs applied.
- Scenario 3 (Large-scale low-risk churn): frequent config heartbeats produce high-volume low-risk events. Sampling engine keeps 0.5% full fidelity and produces compact tokens for the remainder to allow reconstruction if correlated events are later promoted to retained.

Notes to reviewers
- Focus review on the sampling heuristics and the legal/consent implications of proxy-bypass. We expect product + legal + infra alignment before alpha.
- Ping me (Maya) for the simulator dataset; Rafael is owning the capsule signing prototype.

TODOs (owners)
- Prototype capsule signer (Owen) — due: 2025-11-24.
- Simulator runs and recall report (Rafael) — due: 2025-12-05.
- Legal draft (Lina) — due: 2025-11-30.
summary: Draft PRD exploring a policy-driven network fallback system and risk-aware audit log sampling for Private deployments. Prioritizes auditable fallback choices, compact evidence capsules, and customer-configurable sampling to balance availability, cost, and forensic recall.
